articles.headline: European soccer live updates: Brighton humble Premier League champs Arsenal
articles.description: Another weekend of European soccer action continues with Brighton & Hove Albion hosting Premier League leaders and defending champions Arsenal.
articles.body:
It's another weekend of European soccer and the final one before the international break!

In the Premier League, Saturday's action began with Aston Villa beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-2 in London. Both teams were chasing their first league victory of the season and, while Spurs are still winless and in the bottom three, they did score their first goals on the campaign.

Next up, Brighton & Hove Albion welcomed league leaders Arsenal to England's south coast, and promptly dispatched the defending champions 3-0. Finally, Nottingham Forest host a Coventry City side still searching for their first win and goal of the season.

Elsewhere, AS Roma host Inter Milan in a huge clash between Serie A's current top two. In the Bundesliga, Stuttgart take on Borussia Dortmund, while in LaLiga, Sevilla host league leaders Barcelona.

Enjoy all the updates from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: Newcastle end Hull's unbeaten record with early brace
articles.description: Hull's unbeaten start to life in the Premier League came to an end with a 2-1 defeat to Newcastle at St James' Park.
articles.body:
Hull's unbeaten start to life in the Premier League came to an end with a 2-1 defeat to Newcastle at St James' Park.

A pulsating opening saw Joe Willock and Lewis Hall score in the first seven minutes and the Magpies were unable to capitalise on another opportunity to inflict further misery on Hull before the break when Yoane Wissa's penalty was saved.

Substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho pulled one back for the Tigers, but Newcastle managed to withstand a late flurry of attacks from the visitors to seal victory, which comes only five days after a bruising 4-1 defeat to Leeds.

With an increasing injury list to contend with, Matthias Jaissle made two switches from the Leeds defeat as Sean Steur and Willock both started.

Hull also opted for two changes, with Lucas Herrington and Sorba Thomas lining up, the latter of whom was making his first Premier League start.

Willock made an instant impact on his return to the starting 11, having a shot blocked, and moments later sent the Magpies ahead with a low finish past Konstantinos Tzolakis from Harvey Barnes' ball.

Newcastle's ruthless start continued as they doubled their lead only four minutes later, with Barnes once again the provider this time for Hall, who dispatched the ball into the bottom right corner.

Hull began to see more of the ball as Mohamed Belloumi piled pressure on Lukás Hornícek and snatched the ball from his feet, but the goalkeeper recovered.

Matt Crooks' dangerous cross for Thomas was bundled behind for a corner, but the Magpies continued to threaten as Jacob Murphy dragged an effort wide.

The winger sent another shot past the upright and was in the thick of the action again, firing a teasing ball across the box towards Hall, who was unable to stab home.

Newcastle had the opportunity to extend their lead from the penalty spot before the break when Thomas made a grab at Murphy's foot and VAR upheld the onfield decision, but Wissa's spot-kick was pushed away by Tzolakis.

Thomas blasted an effort wide at the end of the half and Tzolakis was called into action after the restart to hold Sven Botman's header from Hall's cross.

Belloumi lifted the ball over the bar moments later and sent another effort over as Hull looked to strike.

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: A+ to F

- Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle hoping for 'positive' update on Anthony Elanga injury

The visitors pulled one back in the 67th minute when Belloumi threaded the ball in for Cho, who scored just four minutes after being introduced as his shot bounced off the post and into the net.

Hull continued to apply pressure when Hornicek parried away Belloumi's effort and following a string of chances aimed towards the Newcastle goal, Tim Iroegbunam sliced a shot narrowly wide of the post.

The momentum was fully with Hull in the final stages as Lucas Gourna-Douath's strike smashed into a crowded box and Joe Gelhardt chipped wide, but the Tynesiders held on.

articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season is off to an exciting start, as the Bills defeated the Lions 41-31 in the first game at Highmark Stadium. But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projected out stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen suggests three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Bengals upset the Texans? Will we see big receiving days for the Dolphins' Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas? Can Eagles running back Saquon Barkley find the end zone? And is it finally time for the Jets to snag an interception? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Jacksonville Jaguars +2.5 at Denver Broncos (+124)

Denver's offense hasn't shown enough to justify laying points. The Broncos produced only 176 yards and 3.7 yards per play in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, with quarterback Bo Nix turning it over twice. Jacksonville is bringing a pass rush that generated five sacks against Cleveland, while QB Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes. Defense makes the Broncos the favorite, but the Jaguars have the more trustworthy offense to win outright.

Cincinnati Bengals +2.5 at Houston Texans (+120)

The Bengals' biggest weakness looked better against the Bucs, as quarterback Joe Burrow was sacked only once. If that holds, he gets a Houston defense that just allowed 10.4 yards per pass to Buffalo in Week 1. Houston can obviously pressure Burrow, but if Cincinnati's offensive line continues to improve, it should have enough through the air with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, New England Patriots: 16 carries, 63 rushing yards; 5 receptions, 42 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown

Since 2023, running backs catch passes on 8% of dropbacks against man coverage but 15% against zone coverage. Why does that matter here? Because in Week 1 against the Falcons, the Steelers ran zone coverage 89% of the time under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. So I expect Stevenson to have a big day in the receiving game.

And while I don't expect the Patriots will be as run-heavy as they were in Week 1 -- which certainly didn't work out for them! -- New England should be ahead by enough early to run the ball late in the game. All in all, it should be a healthy workload for Stevenson.

articles.headline: Man United Muslim Supporters' Club call for Sir Jim Ratcliffe to leave club
articles.description: Manchester United's Muslim Supporters' Club has called for owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to leave the club.
articles.body:
Manchester United's Muslim Supporters' Club has called for owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to leave the club, with his latest comments about immigration coming as the Red Devils struggle on the pitch.

Ratcliffe, who in February said the UK had been "colonised by immigrants" and later apologised if he offended anyone, has this week doubled down on his comments in the BBC's 'Big Boss' interview.

The 73-year-old, who is a resident in Monaco, once again put forward his views on immigration, saying the country "is on the slide" because of it.

Ratcliffe said: "We had the greatest empire in the world. We were a great people.

"We won two world wars. We're good, honest folk. But unfortunately, at the moment, I think the UK is on the slide. It's quite difficult to see how we arrest it.

"Nobody's tough enough to deal with the immigration problem.

"Nobody's tough enough to deal with the benefits problem. But somebody needs to do it."

The MUMSC condemned Ratcliffe's words earlier in the year and have once again spoken out against his latest comments, describing them as "deeply disappointing".

United have suffered a difficult start to the campaign, having lost two games in the Premier League and been knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton in midweek.

Fans protested against the current ownership before their 1-0 defeat to Manchester City last week with a banner that read "the way you treat us is a disgrace," and Ratcliffe's comments on immigration prompted MUMSC to take to X.

Part of the 750-word statement read: "Our players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds.

"Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them. That diversity isn't a weakness of Manchester United. It is part of Manchester United

"Different backgrounds. Different beliefs. Different politics. One Manchester United.

"Manchester United does not belong emotionally to investment funds, shareholders or billionaires. It belongs to the generations of supporters who inherited this club from their parents and grandparents and who will one day pass it to their children.

"We love Manchester United. This club is all we know and, when it comes to football, it will be all we ever know. That is precisely why we cannot stay silent.

"This is bigger than one defeat. Bigger than one manager. Bigger than one season. It is about the direction, leadership and identity of Manchester United Football Club.

"After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club.

"Enough is enough. It is time for change. The Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe must go.

articles.headline: Brighton rout Arsenal to end Premier League champions' 100% record
articles.description: Premier League champions Arsenal lost their 100% record for the season in dramatic fashion as they were routed 3-0 at Brighton and Hove Albion.
articles.body:
Premier League champions Arsenal lost their 100% record for the season in dramatic fashion as they were routed 3-0 at Brighton and Hove Albion.

First-half strikes from Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas put the home side in control at the break, before summer signing Chema Andrés added a third from a corner on his full home debut.

The Spaniard's header meant that Arsenal -- which had been defensively excellent this season -- conceded as many goals on Saturday as they had done in the rest of the season combined.

After a cagey opening on the south coast, the game sparked into life on the half-hour mark when the in-form Gross found himself with time and space on the edge of the box.

Arsenal center backs Gabriel and Ezri Konsa failed to close him down and the German took full advantage, seeing his driven effort crash off David Raya's near post and into the net for Gross' fourth goal in the last five games.

Gabriel and Konsa, normally so solid, made the same mistake again on the stroke of halftime as Kostoulas collected a pass from Diego Gómez, found himself in a similar amount of space and hit a low driven shot between the Arsenal center backs and into the bottom left corner.

Just under 10 minutes into the second half, and just as Arsenal looked like they might be able to mount an unlikely comeback, Brighton put the result beyond all doubt.

Gross was involved again, sending a corner to the back post where Andrés jumped highest to head the ball beyond his compatriot Raya and spark further celebrations at the Amex Stadium.

Arsenal turned to their bench as Mikel Arteta sent on the likes of Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyökeres, but it was Kai Havertz who had the best chance to grab a consolation when he raced clean through on goal only to see his low effort saved by the feet of Bart Verbruggen.

- Brighton vs Arsenal LIVE: Premier League updates as hosts run riot against lackluster Gunners

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal's Madueke eyed by Premier League rivals

- Arsenal, Mikel Arteta open to Max Dowman loan move

It meant that Arsenal lost by three or more goals for the first time since May 2023, when they were beaten 3-0 by none other than Brighton.

Brighton's best win of an already impressive season sees them rise to third in the Premier League table, while Manchester City can go three points clear of Arsenal at the top if they beat Sunderland on Sunday.

articles.headline: Thierno Barry strikes for Everton to sink 10-man Ipswich
articles.description: Abdul Fatawu's dismissal after being shown a second yellow card for diving capped a frustrating afternoon for Ipswich in their 1-0 defeat at Everton.
articles.body:
Abdul Fatawu's dismissal after being shown a second yellow card for diving capped a frustrating afternoon for Ipswich in their 1-0 defeat at Everton.

Having gone behind to Thierno Barry's deflected first-half goal, the visitors then had to chase the game with 10 men for nearly half an hour after the winger's ill-judged choice to throw himself to the ground as he went past James Garner.

Referee Stuart Attwell ruled that was simulation and, having been booked in the first half for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, dismissed the Ghanaian -- although, surprisingly, that was not the most controversial decision by the official.

Having been alerted by VAR, he ruled out Barry's brilliantly-executed second-half header as Brennan Johnson was offside in front of Christian Walton, despite the goalkeeper being in the opposite half of the goal to where the ball entered the net.

That may have curtailed Barry's celebrations but he still proved to be the match-winner, although whether his diversion of the ball with his chest was a clever piece of quick thinking or just fortunate as he tried to get out of the way of James Tarkowski's speculative 30-yard volley very much depends on which camp you are in regarding the 23-year-old.

He has five goals in all competitions this season so supporters will look at that as progress but he still has many who doubt whether he has the rigour or quality to succeed in the Premier League.

That dichotomy was evident later in the first half when, unmarked inside the six-yard box, he planted a header wide when it seemed easier to score.

Yet the technique he produced to flick a delightful header inside the far post, having found half a yard inside a crowded six-yard box at a corner, showed there is talent there to be unlocked.

His goal extended Everton's unbeaten start to the season without the side really clicking into gear yet but their fifth position in the fledgling Premier League table is a good base to build from when David Moyes does start to get a tune out of them.

And there are signs that may yet come with improving form from the likes of Harrison Armstrong, restored to the starting line-up, and Tyler Dibling, who after impressing in the midweek Carabao Cup win over Wolves, could have had a goal and should definitely have had an assist after coming off the bench.

And of course Barry, who continues to delight and frustrate Toffees fans in equal measure.

articles.headline: Arsenal battered by brilliant Brighton to end perfect start
articles.description: Arsenal's 100% start to their Premier League title defence ended in emphatic fashion as Brighton secured a stunning 3-0 win against Mikel Arteta's dumbstruck side.
articles.body:
Arsenal's 100% start to their Premier League title defence ended in emphatic fashion as Brighton secured a stunning 3-0 win against Mikel Arteta's dumbstruck side.

Arsenal arrived at the Amex Stadium with ambitions of equalling a 123-year club record of eight straight victories to start a season, but that piece of history looked in doubt right from the kick-off, with a rampant Brighton side delivering a masterclass against the champions.

Pascal Gross blasted Brighton ahead after 31 minutes before Charalampos Kostoulas doubled the hosts' lead on the stroke of half-time.

Arteta sprinted down the tunnel in the hope of masterminding a half-time speech which would revive his side's fortunes.

But Brighton remained on top after the interval and they served Arsenal a dose of their own medicine when Chema Andrés headed home from a corner shortly before the hour mark.

A disjointed Arsenal were never at the races and Arteta will now have 21 days to stew over a shock result, which will abruptly end any suggestion of his side cantering to a second league title in as many seasons.

For Brighton, surely the best result of manager Fabian Hurzeler's career - just days after a brilliant Carabao Cup comeback win at Manchester United - catapults them up to third in the table, just two points off the Gunners.

Arteta might have rotated his side for their win at Ipswich earlier in the week, but here he fielded his strongest side - one that simply could not live with their inspired opponents.

After just seven minutes Bruno Guimaraes, making his first Premier League start for his new employers, gave the ball away, and Kostoulas tried his luck from range.

David Raya got fingertips to the Brighton man's shot, but it was a sign of things to come.

Arsenal were pegged in by the relentless Seagulls and the hosts' deserved breakthrough arrived.

Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori allowed Gross far too much time to shoot and his fine 20-yard strike pinged in off Raya's near post.

A case could be made for Raya being Arsenal's MVP last season, but the Spaniard should have done better to divert Gross' long-range strike away from danger.

The largely anonymous Bukayo Saka fluffed his lines when he failed to get any meaningful contact on a fine Arsenal counter-attack and Brighton raced straight up the other end to increase their advantage.

Calafiori was out of position and, when the ball fell to Kostoulas, the visitors failed to put any pressure on the Greece forward. He unleashed an unstoppable low strike from 22 yards and Raya was beaten again.

It was virtually the last kick of the first half and Arteta sprinted for the dressing room ahead of a pivotal team-talk, with Arsenal's 100% record hanging in the balance, and then some.

And Andres all but ended any hope of a comeback when he leapt unmarked from a corner to head a third for Brighton with 57 minutes on the clock.

articles.headline: Deco confirms Barcelona contract extensions for Raphinha, Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart
articles.description: Barcelona sporting director Deco has confirmed agreements to extend Raphinha, Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart's contracts.
articles.body:
Barcelona sporting director Deco has confirmed agreements to extend Raphinha, Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart's contracts.

Raphinha, 29, will extend his contract until 2030 after an explosive start to the season playing as a striker.

The Brazilian, whose previous deal was due to expire in 2028, has scored 11 goals in seven appearances to plug the gap left by Robert Lewandowski.

His performances have earned him extended terms, with Deco confirming an agreement was reached with the forward this past week.

It is one of three new deals Deco has negotiated since the closing of the transfer window earlier this month.

Youngsters Bernal and Espart will both also sign renewals in the coming days, Deco confirmed.

- Raphinha bags hat trick as Barcelona score 7 to set record start

- Mourinho rejects Real Madrid, Barcelona comparisons: LaLiga 'a marathon'

- Yamal says he has experienced racism 'a thousand times'

Bernal, 19, will sign until 2031 after emerging as the first alternate to midfield duo Pedri and Rodri at the start of the new campaign.

Espart, also 19, will pen new terms until 2030 after breaking into the first team permanently this summer.

The youngster came through La Masia as a midfielder, made his debut under Hansi Flick as a right-back last season and has been used as a left-back this term.

Espart's performances have kept both João Cancelo and Alejandro Balde out the team for the majority of the season so far.

Both Bernal and Espart are from Barça's incredible 2007 generation, which also includes Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí.

Sept. 19: Saturday morning's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's action starts a bit earlier than initially scheduled, with the Windy City doubling as Rainy City. To avoid heavy showers in the early evening, the Chicago White Sox hosting the Detroit Tigers has been moved up to 2:10 p.m. ET. Three more matinees follow in the 4:00 p.m. ET block, leaving 11 evening games.

The Boston Red Sox have not quite yet secured a playoff berth, but they're adjusting their rotation for the impending wild-card round by sending Brayan Bello to the hill today to face the Tampa Bay Rays in St. Petersburg. A Red Sox win alone doesn't clinch a postseason spot, but a win combined with a Texas Rangers loss, or if the Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays and the Atlanta Braves defeat the Houston Astros, the Red Sox will make the wild-card round for the second straight season.

The New York Yankees are set to place Aaron Judge on the 10-day IL due to a right calf strain. Backdating the visit to Wednesday will allow the slugger to return for the last day of the season, though it's unclear if he'll be ready. His playoff availability is also in jeopardy. Heliot Ramos will likely see more action in right field.

Hunter Goodman rejoined the Colorado Rockies lineup after missing four of the past five games. He's been nursing a sore thumb. Goodman enters the weekend leading all catchers in home runs with 38.

Dansby Swanson was reinstated from the injured list in advance of last night's game between the Chicago Cubs and Cincinnati Reds. The slick-fielding shortstop's return pushed Nico Hoerner back to second base. Swanson is two home runs and three steals away from a 20/20 season, but his .217 batting average is by far the lowest of his career.

The St. Louis Cardinals will have to play the rest of the season without Joshua Baez. He was placed on the 10-day IL with a strained left oblique. Technically, he can return for the final game of the season, but chances are he won't be ready.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Saturday.
